title: Callout Overlay Anatomy Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Image Overlays
Callout Labels
JSON
Data-Driven Design
description: A p5.js MicroSim that shows a text-free animal cell with four callout markers beside the overlay data file as syntax-colored JSON, so learners can see how x, y, label, hint and description become marker positions, labels, quiz clues and an information box, including why positions are stored as percentages.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Fields of the overlay data file and how the callout engine renders them
learningObjectives: The learner will explain how each field of an overlay data file (position, label, hint, description) appears in the rendered overlay, by changing one field and observing the effect.
prerequisites: Callout labels, point markers and the overlay data file (Chapter 10)

accessibility.notes: describe() is updated with the current mode and selection; sliders and mode buttons are native controls; markers carry numbers as well as colors

dataFiles: Overlay data object (title, image, callouts[]) embedded in callout-overlay-anatomy-explorer.js

controls.label: Callout markers 1-4
controls.purpose: Hover to highlight the leader line, JSON block and description; click to select (Explore) or answer (Quiz)

controls.label: Explore
controls.purpose: Show labels and allow editing positions

controls.label: Quiz
controls.purpose: Hide labels and ask for the marker matching each hint

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Change one field and observe; side-by-side data and rendering
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Linked views (picture and JSON) with sliders and a hint quiz
keyQuestions: Which part of the overlay does each field of the data file control?
Why are marker positions stored as percentages instead of pixels?
Why does the hint describe a structure without naming it?
commonMisconceptions: Labels are part of the image (they live only in the data file)
x and y are pixel coordinates (they are percentages of the image size)
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz score on the hint-to-marker questions
Written mapping of each field to its on-screen element
